questions.stem: A 26/M presented with progressive dyspnea on exertion for 5 months. He is a stone crusher. He had a long‐standing cough with whitish sputum production, but denied fever, chills, weight loss, night sweats, and other symptoms. The patient undergoes bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage. The effluent appears milky. The cytopathology shows amorphous debris with periodic acid-Schiff (PAS)–positive macrophages. What is the diagnosis?
